title: FiatRecord.at is empty in the store for every kind, and never stamped at all for ST and WP
body:
AC-00.2 requires the fiat record to carry its timestamp and survive the store-to-extract-to-store round trip. DRIVEN 2026-08-30 (dc): it does not. TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS IN ONE FIELD.

DEFECT 1 -- THE PATCH REACHES THE EXTRACT AND NEVER THE STORE (AC and AT records).

`apply_envelopes` commits the mutation, THEN walks `next.threads[].criteria[].state` and `next.threads[].tests[].fiat` patching `record.at = dates.event_ts`, THEN renders the projection. So the extract is rendered from the patched value and the store row was written from the pre-patch one.

  canon immediately after `fc`   at = 2026-08-30T12:11:50.743Z
  event_log ac.fc ts             2026-08-30T12:11:50.743Z    (equal -- D42 honoured)
  store row                      at = ""
  canon after `sync --to-disk`   at = ""                     (the good value overwritten)

SO THE TIMESTAMP IS DESTROYED BY THE NEXT SYNC, AND IT INVERTS THE SSOT. D01 makes the DB durable truth; here the only correct copy lives in the DERIVED artefact and the authoritative one overwrites it with a blank. The patch loop's own comment names this exact failure -- "Rendering the extract before this point would write an empty string into the one field neither truth nor its projection can recompute" -- and the ordering it guards against is the one that ships.

DEFECT 2 -- `thread.fiat` AND `wp.fiat` ARE NEVER STAMPED AT ALL, NOT EVEN IN THE EXTRACT.

The patch loop walks `criteria` and `tests` only. Driven, canon immediately after `fc`, no sync:
  fc ST0001/01   wp.fiat.at = ""    (cascaded AC-01.1 at = 2026-08-30T12:12:47.836Z, inherited_from ST0001/01)
  fc ST0001      thread.fiat.at = ""  (both cascaded ACs stamped correctly)

So a thread or package closed on authority carries no record of WHEN, on any surface, ever.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT. `fiat_close_is_stamped_by_the_database.rs` drives the facade and reads the state back THROUGH THE SAME IN-PROCESS FACADE, after the patch -- it never re-reads from the store, so it is blind to persistence. Its own doc claims it is two-sided by construction: "remove the patch loop and `at` is the empty string it was handed in as". True of the in-memory value and silent about the persisted one. The round-trip is also byte-faithful AFTER the first sync, because empty round-trips to empty -- so a round-trip test passes on a record whose stamp has already been destroyed. And no render displays `at`, so no view test sees it either.

CONSEQUENCE: AC-00.2 STAYS UNSATISFIED. It is not a rendering gap; the field the row names is absent from durable truth for every kind and absent everywhere for two of them.
